Tafsir of Surah al-Qari'ah (The Striking Calamity)

It is Makki.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿The Striking Calamity﴾ is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, like al-Haqqah (The Inevitable Reality), at-Tammah (The Overwhelming Calamity), as-Sakhkhah (The Deafening Blast), al-Ghashiyah (The Overwhelming Event), and others.

Then He said, magnifying its matter and emphasising its greatness: ﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾ Then He explained it with His saying: ﴿It is a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾, meaning: in their dispersal and scattering, their going and coming, out of their bewilderment at what they are in, as if they were scattered moths. [[In A: "scattered" (munتashir).]] As He said in the other verse: ﴿as if they were scattered locusts﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be like wool fluffed out﴾ means: they will have become like fluffed-out wool that has begun to fly away and disintegrate.

Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: "al-'Ihn" is wool.

Then Allah, the Exalted, informed of what the deeds of the doers will lead to, and what they will come to of honour or humiliation according to their deeds, saying: ﴿As for him whose scales are heavy﴾, meaning: whose good deeds outweigh his evil deeds, ﴿he will be in a pleasant life﴾, meaning: in Paradise. ﴿But as for him whose scales are light﴾, meaning: whose evil deeds outweigh his good deeds.

* *

And His saying: ﴿His mother will be the Pit﴾. It was said: its meaning is: he will fall headlong into the Fire of Hell, with his head down. This is expressed by "his mother", meaning his brain. This was narrated similarly from Ibn 'Abbas, Ikrimah, Abu Salih and Qatadah. Qatadah said: he will plunge into the Fire on his head. Likewise Abu Salih said: they will plunge into the Fire on their heads.

It was also said: its meaning is: ﴿his mother﴾ is the one to whom he returns, and to whom he goes in the Hereafter, ﴿the Pit﴾, which is one of the names of the Fire.

Ibn Jarir said: The Pit is called his mother only because he has no refuge other than it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/183).]]

Ibn Zayd said: al-Hawiyah is the Fire; it is his mother and his refuge to which he returns and in which he takes shelter. And he recited: ﴿And their refuge is the Fire﴾ [Al 'Imran: 151].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is narrated from Qatadah that he said: it is the Fire, and it is their refuge. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said, explaining the Pit: ﴿And what will make you know what it is? A blazing Fire﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Ash'ath ibn 'Abd Allah al-A'ma, who said: When the believer dies, his soul is taken to the souls of the believers, and they say: "Make your brother rest, for he was in the distress of the world." He said: And they ask him: "What has so-and-so done?" He says: "He has died," or, "Has he not come to you?" They say: "He has been taken to his mother, the Pit." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/182).]]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Anas ibn Malik, traced to the Prophet, in a fuller form than this. We have included it in the book Sifat al-Nar (The Description of the Fire); may Allah protect us from it by His bounty and generosity. [[Al-Suyuti said in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/606): "Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'When the believer dies, the souls of the believers meet him and ask him: What has so-and-so done? What has so-and-so done? If he had died and not come to them, they say: He has been taken to his mother, the Pit; what an evil mother and an evil nurse. Then they say: What has so-and-so done, has he married? What has so-and-so done, has she married? They say: Leave him, let him rest, for he has come out of the distress of the world.'"]].

* *

And His saying: ﴿a blazing Fire﴾, meaning: intensely hot, of fierce heat, with strong flames and blaze.

Abu Mus'ab narrated from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The fire of the children of Adam which you kindle is one part of seventy parts of the Fire of Hell." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, it would surely be sufficient." He said: "It has been given precedence over it by sixty-nine parts." [[Muwatta' Malik, narration of al-Zuhri, no. (2098), and in the narration of Yahya (2/994).]]

al-Bukhari narrated it from Isma'il ibn Abi Uways, from Malik. Muslim narrated it from Qutaybah, from al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Zinad, with the same. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3265) and Sahih Muslim no. (2843).]] In some of its wording: "It has been given precedence over it by sixty-nine parts, all of them like its heat."

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, namely Ibn Salamah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) say: "The fire of the children of Adam which you kindle is one part of seventy parts of the Fire of Hell." A man said: "It would surely be sufficient." He said: "It has been given precedence over it by sixty-nine parts, each one as hot as the other." [[Musnad (2/467).]]

Ahmad alone narrated it by this route, and it is according to the condition of Muslim.

Imam Ahmad also said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and 'Amr, from Yahya ibn Ja'dah: "Your fire is indeed one part of seventy parts of the Fire of Hell, and it was struck in the sea twice, and were it not for that, Allah would not have placed in it any benefit for anyone." [[Musnad (2/244).]]

This is according to the condition of authenticity, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it by this route. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih by the route of Ibn Abi al-Zinad. [[Sahih Muslim no. (2843).]]

al-Bazzar narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: "Your fire is one part of seventy parts." [[As for the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, it is in Musnad al-Bazzar no. (1864), by the route of 'Ubayd ibn Ishaq, from Zuhayr, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Bazzar said: "Zuhayr narrated it thus, and we do not know anyone who narrated it from Zuhayr except 'Ubayd ibn Ishaq. 'Amr ibn Thabit narrated it from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr al-Asamm, from 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) similarly, and others apart from 'Amr ibn Thabit narrated it from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr al-Asamm, from 'Abd Allah, as a mawquf (halted) report." As for the hadith of Abu Sa'id, al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in his Sunan no. (2590) by the route of Firas, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Qutaybah narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, namely Ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "This fire is one part of a hundred parts of Hell." [[Musnad (2/379).]]

He alone narrated it by this route, and it is also according to the condition of Muslim.

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn 'Amr al-Khallal narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami narrated to us, Ma'n ibn 'Isa al-Qazzaz narrated to us, from Malik, from his paternal uncle Abu Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what the likeness of this fire of yours is compared to the fire of Hell? It is far blacker than the smoke of this fire of yours by seventy times." [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. (4843) "Majma' al-Bahrayn"; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/387): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

Abu Mus'ab narrated it from Malik, but did not trace it to the Prophet. al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated from 'Abbas al-Duri, from Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr: Sharik narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Fire was kindled for a thousand years until it became red, then it was kindled for a thousand years until it became white, then it was kindled for a thousand years until it became black, so it is black and dark." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2591) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4320). al-Tirmidhi said: "The hadith of Abu Hurayrah on this is more authentic as a mawquf report, and I know of no one who traced it to the Prophet except Yahya ibn Bukayr from Sharik."]]

This has been narrated also from the hadith of Anas and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. [[The hadith of Anas was narrated by Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman by the route of Mubarak ibn Fadalah, from Thabit, from Anas, traced to the Prophet, and it was mentioned earlier in the commentary on verse 81 of Surah al-Tawbah.]]

And there came in a hadith, in the narration of Imam Ahmad, by the route of Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Anas, and Abu Nadrah al-'Abdi, from Abu Sa'id, and 'Ajlan, mawla of al-Mushma'il, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed, the least punished of the people of the Fire is the one who has two sandals, from which his brain boils." [[The hadith of Abu Sa'id is in al-Musnad (3/13) and the hadith of Abu Hurayrah is in al-Musnad (2/432).]]

It is established in the Sahih [[In M: "in the Two Sahihs."]] that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Fire complained to its Lord, saying: 'O Lord, some of me has consumed other parts of me.' So He permitted it two breaths: a breath in winter and a breath in summer. So the most intense cold you find is from its chill, and the most intense heat you find in summer is from its heat." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3260), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

In the Two Sahihs: "When the heat intensifies, delay the prayer until it cools, for the intensity of the heat is from the exhalation of Hell." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (533) and Sahih Muslim no. (615), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

End of the Tafsir of Surah "al-Qari'ah".

Tafsir of Surah al-Qari'ah (The Striking Calamity)

It is Makki.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿The Striking Calamity﴾ is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, like al-Haqqah (The Inevitable Reality), at-Tammah (The Overwhelming Calamity), as-Sakhkhah (The Deafening Blast), al-Ghashiyah (The Overwhelming Event), and others.

Then He said, magnifying its matter and emphasising its greatness: ﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾ Then He explained it with His saying: ﴿It is a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾, meaning: in their dispersal and scattering, their going and coming, out of their bewilderment at what they are in, as if they were scattered moths. [[In A: "scattered" (munتashir).]] As He said in the other verse: ﴿as if they were scattered locusts﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be like wool fluffed out﴾ means: they will have become like fluffed-out wool that has begun to fly away and disintegrate.

Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: "al-'Ihn" is wool.

Then Allah, the Exalted, informed of what the deeds of the doers will lead to, and what they will come to of honour or humiliation according to their deeds, saying: ﴿As for him whose scales are heavy﴾, meaning: whose good deeds outweigh his evil deeds, ﴿he will be in a pleasant life﴾, meaning: in Paradise. ﴿But as for him whose scales are light﴾, meaning: whose evil deeds outweigh his good deeds.

* *

And His saying: ﴿His mother will be the Pit﴾. It was said: its meaning is: he will fall headlong into the Fire of Hell, with his head down. This is expressed by "his mother", meaning his brain. This was narrated similarly from Ibn 'Abbas, Ikrimah, Abu Salih and Qatadah. Qatadah said: he will plunge into the Fire on his head. Likewise Abu Salih said: they will plunge into the Fire on their heads.

It was also said: its meaning is: ﴿his mother﴾ is the one to whom he returns, and to whom he goes in the Hereafter, ﴿the Pit﴾, which is one of the names of the Fire.

Ibn Jarir said: The Pit is called his mother only because he has no refuge other than it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/183).]]

Ibn Zayd said: al-Hawiyah is the Fire; it is his mother and his refuge to which he returns and in which he takes shelter. And he recited: ﴿And their refuge is the Fire﴾ [Al 'Imran: 151].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is narrated from Qatadah that he said: it is the Fire, and it is their refuge. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said, explaining the Pit: ﴿And what will make you know what it is? A blazing Fire﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Ash'ath ibn 'Abd Allah al-A'ma, who said: When the believer dies, his soul is taken to the souls of the believers, and they say: "Make your brother rest, for he was in the distress of the world." He said: And they ask him: "What has so-and-so done?" He says: "He has died," or, "Has he not come to you?" They say: "He has been taken to his mother, the Pit." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/182).]]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Anas ibn Malik, traced to the Prophet, in a fuller form than this. We have included it in the book Sifat al-Nar (The Description of the Fire); may Allah protect us from it by His bounty and generosity. [[Al-Suyuti said in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/606): "Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'When the believer dies, the souls of the believers meet him and ask him: What has so-and-so done?
